Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: kasvihuo: Schematic diagram, not to scale: the greenhouse effect. The Sun's radiation (orange arrow), visible light and near-infrared, passes mostly through the atmosphere and warms the ground. The warm ground sends thermal radiation upwards (red arrows), and the greenhouse gases of the atmosphere absorb it. The gases radiate the energy out again: part returns down to the ground and part escapes into space. The thickness of the arrows illustrates direction, not exact energies.
Vaakapylväskaavio sähköntuotannon elinka: Horizontal bar chart of the life-cycle emission factors of electricity production in the unit g of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilowatt-hour (IPCC AR5, Working Group III, Annex III, rounded medians): coal 820, natural gas 490, biomass 230, solar power 41–48, hydropower 24, nuclear power 12 and wind power 11–12. The lengths of the bars are to scale: the bar for coal is about 70 times as long as the bar for nuclear power. The bars of fossil fuels are dark grey and those of the other ways of producing energy light grey; the legend is below the figure.
